items.title: Pemberdayaan Pokdarwis Melalui Layanan Suara Berbasis AI di Desa Wisata Kelawi
items.abstract: Kelawi Tourism Village, South Lampung, has strong community-based tourism potential, but the Minang Rua Bahari Tourism Awareness Group (Pokdarwis) faces communication barriers when serving international visitors. This Community Service Program (PKM) aimed to strengthen Pokdarwis capacity through an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted voice service as a communication support tool. The program was conducted from 12 to 14 June 2026 and involved 15 Pokdarwis members. Activities included problem identification, local knowledge development and validation, QR-based service implementation, training, mentoring, and evaluation at four service points: visitor reception, turtle conservation, Green Canyon, and homestay and culinary services. Results showed an increase in partner capacity from 58.2% in the pre-test to 91.8% in the post-test, representing a 33.6 percentage-point improvement. Participant satisfaction reached 92%, while partner and visitor achievement rates reached 95.2% and 94.5%, respectively. The program demonstrates that AI can support communication, conservation, safety, and the delivery of local cultural and culinary information without replacing the role of Pokdarwis.

items.title: Perceptions of Academic Staff on the Integration of AI and Digital Connectivity for Transformative Educational Management in Bayelsa State
items.abstract: The study assessed the perceptions of academic staff on the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digital connectivity for transformative educational management in tertiary institutions in Bayelsa State. A descriptive survey research design was adopted, guided by two research questions. The population comprised academic staff from selected public universities and colleges of education in Bayelsa State, from which a sample of 350 respondents was drawn using stratified random sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire titled Artificial Intelligence and Digital Connectivity in Educational Management Questionnaire (AIDEMQ), validated by experts and yielding a reliability coefficient of 0.89 via Cronbach's alpha. Descriptive statistics (mean and standard deviation) were used to answer the research questions. The findings revealed that academic staff generally perceived AI as enhancing administrative efficiency through improved decision-making, error reduction, transparency, and time management, although challenges such as inadequate training and limited practical application constrained its full potential. Similarly, digital connectivity was perceived as effective in improving communication, collaboration, information dissemination, and the quality of teaching and learning, though gaps in infrastructure and system functionality limited its impact on administrative planning and scheduling. The study concluded that while AI and digital connectivity hold significant potential for transforming educational management, targeted interventions including capacity building, infrastructure enhancement, and strategic system integration are necessary to fully realize these benefits. Recommendations included providing regular staff training, investing in robust digital infrastructure, and implementing supportive policies to optimize the integration of AI and digital tools in tertiary institutions.

items.title: Persistent Agent Memory under the EU AI Act and NIS2: Misalignment, Emergent Behaviour and Regulatory Fit
items.abstract: Abstract Agentic AI systems commonly combine a general-purpose AI model with prompts, tools, orchestration and an external memory layer. The model need not be fine-tuned: records retrieved from persistent memory are normally inserted into the model’s inference-time context and can thereby influence later outputs and actions without changing model weights. This article asks how far the EU Artificial Intelligence Act and Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2) already govern the risks that follow. It reframes persistent memory as a system feature that can mediate or amplify misalignment and emergent behaviour, rather than as training data or a new category in the AI Act’s use-case-based taxonomy. Article 15 provides a clear legal anchor for robustness and cybersecurity, while Articles 9–14, 25, 72 and 73 extend coverage across risk management, data governance, logging, oversight, value-chain responsibility and post-market monitoring. For organisations within NIS2’s scope, Articles 20, 21 and 23 add entity-level governance, all-hazards cybersecurity, supply-chain controls and incident reporting. The remaining problem is therefore not a wholesale absence of law. It is whether these overlapping duties are sufficiently operationalised for memory-mediated failures such as poisoned retrieval, scope leakage, stale reliance, revocation failure and loss of provenance. The article proposes proportionate implementation through existing guidance, standards, documentation and monitoring mechanisms, without creating a new statutory risk tier or a memory-specific regulatory regime.

items.title: Physicians' perceptions of artificial intelligence in clinical and academic practice: a mixed-methods study from Erbil City
items.abstract: Background and objective: Integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare and medical research represents significant potential; however, it also introduces practical and ethical challenges. This study analyzes physicians' perceptions of AI implementation in clinical and academic settings, exploring their awareness, perceptions, barriers, concerns, and insights into ethical and regulatory considerations. Methods: A mixed-methods approach was used. The quantitative component involved standardized surveys completed by 390 physicians (241 clinical, 149 academic) in Erbil City from November 2024 to June 2025. Participants were selected using systematic sampling, and surveys were self-administered. The qualitative component included two focus group discussions, involving 6 clinical physicians and 8 academic physicians, to explore in-depth perceptions and concerns regarding AI in healthcare and research. Results: Of 390 physicians, the majority of participants were male (69.2%). Mean age was 46.7±7 years. Familiarity with AI was higher among younger, male, and academic physicians, with age showing a negative association (p <0.001). Clinical physicians reported more concerns regarding privacy in healthcare (p=0.003) and research (p=0.041), as well as algorithmic bias (p=0.030). Despite these concerns, most physicians valued AI in healthcare and academic research and demonstrated strong interest in training and collaboration. Qualitative findings showed optimism and frequent use of AI tools such as ChatGPT and DeepSeek, often described as “Google replacements.” However, physicians also highlighted ethical issues and the need for local training and infrastructure improvement. Conclusion: Physicians generally welcome the use of AI in healthcare and research but emphasize the necessity of ethical guidelines, peer collaboration, and formal education. To ensure responsible adoption, addressing infrastructural and trust barriers will be essential for guaranteeing that AI technologies improve rather than undermine patient care and research integrity.

items.title: Physics-guided interpretable machine learning for explicit resistance equation discovery in concrete penetration
items.abstract: Classical Forrestal penetration calculations are attractive because they are explicit, but their empirical strength-only resistance term is too restrictive for heterogeneous concrete-penetration data. This study derives a closed-form resistance equation from a governed literature dataset, reducing 497 raw records from 41 source blocks to 443 useable records from 37 sources through duplicate removal, governed density completion, deep-penetration filtering, and descriptor-only anomaly screening. Forrestal inversion maps each measured penetration depth to an operator-consistent effective resistance target described by mechanics-informed dimensionless descriptors. The artificial-intelligence contribution is a constrained equation-discovery workflow in which a categorical gradient-boosting model learns the nonlinear resistance surface, Shapley additive explanations restrict the analytical term family, and limited-memory Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno optimization with bound constraints identifies equation coefficients under a forward penetration-depth objective. The engineering contribution is a 16-term explicit resistance law that replaces the empirical resistance relation inside the Forrestal operator while retaining its deterministic calculation form. On the 89-record held-out set, the equation gives a coefficient of determination of 0.9543 and a mean absolute percentage error of 14.88%, compared with 0.9206 and 24.44% for classical Forrestal and 0.9551 and 13.95% for the nonlinear resistance-reference model; its mean prediction-to-measurement ratio is 0.984. Repeated random, source-grouped, strength-stratified, out-of-distribution, input-uncertainty, and density-robustness tests bound the useable domain. The 80–120 MPa interval remains cautionary because of weaker held-out accuracy and limited cross-source support.

items.title: Power Must Serve Life: New Human Rights as a Rigorous Framework for Political Critique and Accountability
items.abstract: This conceptual working paper examines how Jean-Pol Martin’s New Human Rights (NHR) can serve as a rigorous framework for political critique and accountability. Its normative criterion is the preservation and flourishing of human life, assessed through six equally ranked basic needs: thinking, health, security, social belonging, self-realization and participation, and meaning. Drawing on three complementary theoretical prompts, the paper addresses diplomatic and personal rapprochement with Vladimir Putin, the proposed livestreaming of an execution in the United States, and insufficient climate action. It distinguishes documented events, normative judgments and explanatory hypotheses. What is new in this article is the explicit formulation of the NHR’s political firmness: personal loyalty, public displays of authority and short-term interests must be assessed against their consequences for affected people. The paper translates this principle into a practical procedure involving evidence, participation, public justification and correction of harmful decisions. Within the series, the article connects the anthropological and systemic foundations of the NHR with concrete political evaluation. It extends the discussion of the right to think, human-AI collaboration and ecological responsibility toward institutional accountability. Prepared by Jean-Pol Martin in collaboration with ChatGPT. The paper includes an abstract, theoretical foundations, three illustrative applications, an accountability procedure and references. Current-event evidence is dated to 12 October 2026.

items.title: Pragmatics-zombies
items.abstract: Abstract This paper examines theoretical aspects of human-AI communication, arguing that current AI systems, or ‘pragmatics-zombies,’ can mimic human-like pragmatic competence without genuine understanding. While these systems are increasingly adept at natural language interaction, their lack of subjective experience, intentionality, and embodied cognition creates a fundamental trust deficit, particularly in high-stakes scenarios. We argue that forcing human-to-human pragmatic frameworks onto these non-human entities is suboptimal, leading to issues in efficiency, robustness, and transparency. To address this, we introduce the concept of ‘Abstract Pragmatics,’ a general framework that allows for multiple, distinct pragmatic systems. We propose that instead of pursuing flawless mimicry of human communication, research should focus on developing novel, alternative pragmatic systems specifically designed for human-AI interaction. This approach would prioritize clarity, verifiability, and trustworthiness, fostering a more effective and reliable collaboration between humans and artificial intelligence by acknowledging and adapting to the unique nature of the machine.

items.title: Precision Oncofertility: Integrating Genomics, Reproductive Biomarkers, Treatment Toxicity Profiles, and Foundation Models for Fertility Preservation in Men and Women with Cancer
items.abstract: Background: Cancer survivors of reproductive age face substantial risks of treatment-induced gonadotoxicity, yet clinical decision-making for fertility preservation remains largely empirical and population-based.A precision oncofertility framework that integrates genomic, biomarker, and toxicity data is urgently needed.Objective: To develop and validate a multimodal foundation model that integrates genomic variants, sex-specific reproductive biomarkers, treatment toxicity profiles, and clinical variables to predict fertility impairment risk and support individualized fertility-preservation decisions in cancer patients.Methods: A retrospective observational cohort of 400 patients (age 18-45 years) diagnosed with breast cancer, lymphoma, leukemia, testicular cancer, ovarian cancer, cervical cancer, or colorectal cancer was assembled.All patients received fertility-preservation counselling prior to treatment.Data included reproductive biomarkers (anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), antral follicle count (AFC), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), estradiol; sperm concentration, motility, testosterone, inhibin-B), genomic features (BRCA1, BRCA2, CHEK2, TP53, FMR1), treatment toxicity variables (alkylating agent and platinum exposure, radiation dose, stem cell transplantation), and standard clinical covariates.A transformer-based foundation model with four specialised encoders and cross-modal attention was developed.Performance was benchmarked against Random Forest, XGBoost, and a Deep Neural Network using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC).Results: The foundation model achieved the highest performance across all metrics: accuracy 0.883, precision 0.876, recall 0.862, F1 0.869, and AUC 0.934.AMH (importance score 0.187), AFC (0.171), and alkylating agent exposure (0.152) were the strongest predictors.Fertility risk stratification identified 37.0% (n=148) low-risk, 35.5% (n=142) moderate-risk, and 27.5% (n=110) high-risk patients.BRCA1/2 mutations and radiation dose independently amplified impairment risk.Conclusion: A precision oncofertility framework incorporating multimodal data and transformer-based architecture substantially outperforms conventional machine-learning approaches.AI-guided risk stratification can enable individualized, evidence-based fertility-preservation counselling and intervention, with direct implications for clinical oncofertility practice.

items.title: Preparing Future Outstanding Engineers: Multidimensional Structure and Associated Factors of Core Competence
items.abstract: Preparing engineers for rapidly changing sociotechnical environments requires a clear account of the competencies that undergraduate engineering programs should foster. This study used the term future outstanding engineers to refer to engineering undergraduates being prepared for engineering excellence and examined the structure and correlates of their self-reported core competence. Cross-sectional survey data were obtained from 578 engineering undergraduates at a Chinese research university. A reflective–formative higher-order model was estimated using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM); partial least squares multigroup analysis (PLS-MGA) compared grade cohorts; and multiple linear regression examined associations with student background and educational experience. Adaptive, professional, and basic competence formed the higher-order construct, with adaptive competence receiving the largest outer weight. The outer weight of adaptive competence was larger, and that of professional competence smaller, among third-year than first-year students; the outer weight of basic competence did not differ significantly. Selected co-curricular and language-learning experiences were associated with adaptive competence, whereas family background and leadership experience were associated with professional competence. Basic competence was associated with a broader set of student background and engagement variables. These findings support a differentiated, stage-sensitive approach to competence development. Because the data are cross-sectional, self-reported, and drawn from one institution, the results should be interpreted as structural and associational rather than developmental or causal.

items.title: Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) Laboratory Manual: Fundamentals and Practical Industrial Automation
items.abstract: This PLC Laboratory Manual is an educational and practical resource designed to support undergraduate learning in Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) and industrial automation. The material combines fundamental theoretical concepts with laboratory-oriented procedures to help students understand PLC architecture, programming principles, input/output systems, control logic, and practical automation applications.The manual introduces students to PLC hardware and software environments and provides structured laboratory activities that emphasize practical implementation, testing, simulation, monitoring, and troubleshooting. It also supports the development of essential skills in ladder logic programming, digital and analog I/O handling, control sequencing, timers and counters, and the integration of PLCs with industrial devices and automation systems.Each laboratory activity is organized to connect theoretical concepts with hands-on engineering practice, enabling students to gradually develop the ability to design, implement, test, and evaluate PLC-based control solutions. The material is intended to strengthen students’ understanding of industrial control systems while promoting problem-solving, logical thinking, and practical automation skills.This resource is suitable for undergraduate students, instructors, and learners in Automation, Artificial Intelligence, Systems Engineering, Control Engineering, Mechatronics, and related engineering disciplines who are interested in gaining practical experience with PLC-based industrial automation.The laboratory material can be used as a teaching resource for university laboratory sessions, practical training, and introductory study of programmable control systems and modern industrial automation.

items.title: Promoting Adolescent Health and Confidence: Novel Seamless Sports Bra Design for Comfort, Biomechanical Support, and Satisfaction
items.abstract: The lack of well-fitting and supportive sports bras is a significant public health barrier, hindering adolescent girls from engaging in physical activity and negatively impacting their physical and mental health. This study aims to optimize sports bra design through seamless construction to improve aesthetics, comfort, support, and user satisfaction. A comparative analysis between proposed seamless designs and conventional sports bras evaluated anthropometric fit, biomechanical pressure distribution, and subjective user feedback. The proposed seamless design outperformed the conventional bras in both objective and subjective measures. It received high subjective ratings for support and satisfaction and provided favourable breast shaping. All measured pressures were within a comfortable threshold (<0.96 kPa), and arm movement significantly influenced breast morphology, underscoring the need for dynamic design considerations. The customized seamless knitted design provided smooth aesthetic, adaptive fit, and superior comfort while maintaining robust support, yielding high satisfaction among adolescent users. Bra D2 received the highest satisfaction rating, whereas D3 was the most preferred overall and provided the most favourable balance of comfort, support, coverage, and cushioning. Pearson’s correlation analysis revealed significant associations between specific breast anthropometric parameters (CIBP-OBP, CSNP-SP, HRBP-LBP, HRMSP-LMSP, VFNP-BP) and contact pressure distribution, providing a scientific basis for future pattern engineering. These findings demonstrate that ergonomically optimized seamless sports bras can mitigate the biomechanical barrier to adolescent sports participation.

items.title: Prompt Design as AI-Mediated Pedagogical Performance in Initial Teacher Education: A Case Study in Foreign Language Teaching Methodology
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is creating new possibilities for educational resource development, making prompt design increasingly relevant to interactions with these tools. However, little research has examined how pedagogical criteria are represented in prompts developed within initial teacher education or how prompt design can be conceptualised in relation to teachers’ professional knowledge. This study analyses 15 group-produced prompts and their documented development processes, created by students enrolled in a Bachelor’s Degree in Early Childhood Education during a Foreign Language Teaching Methodology activity involving the creation of children’s stories in English using generative artificial intelligence. An exploratory case study design was adopted, using an eight-dimension analytical rubric addressing pedagogical, linguistic, narrative, and strategic aspects of prompt design, with the corpus independently assessed by three raters. The analysis combined descriptive scores across rubric dimensions with qualitative examination of prompt content and documented revision processes to identify recurring patterns of educational prompt design. Findings showed that educational criteria were generally represented explicitly across the corpus, although differences emerged across dimensions and cases. Strategic development and agency, target learners and language level, and language function and objectives were the most consistently represented dimensions, whereas formal control of the output showed comparatively lower scores and professional contextualisation showed the greatest variability. The combined quantitative and qualitative analysis revealed recurring cross-case patterns in the explicitness and integration of pedagogical criteria rather than discrete competence levels or developmental categories. The findings suggest that prompt design can be examined as a form of AI-mediated pedagogical performance in which educational criteria are translated into operational instructions for generative systems. Rather than demonstrating a wholly independent teaching competence, the study highlights prompt design as a potentially relevant context for mobilising and externalising pedagogical knowledge within initial teacher education. Given the small, context-specific corpus of collaborative prompts, the findings are exploratory and are not intended to support generalisation to individual prompting competence or to other teacher education contexts.

items.title: Protein Language Models, Structure, and Retrieval for VUS Interpretation: A Scoping Review, a Layered Evidence Framework, and a Preliminary Evaluation of One Computational Layer
items.abstract: Variants of uncertain significance (VUS) remain the main obstacle to acting on genetic test results. Protein language models (pLMs), predicted structures, and retrieval-augmented LLMs are usually evaluated separately, often on data overlapping their training or calibration sources, and rarely mapped to calibrated ACMG/AMP evidence strength. This study conducted an interim, abstract-based scoping review (reported following PRISMA-ScR, with deviations) of pLM-, structure-, and LLM/retrieval-based missense interpretation. It proposed a five-layer evidence framework in which a rule-based layer, not the language model, assigns capped evidence strength, and evaluated only one-layer (L1: AlphaMissense and ESM1b in BRCA1) against multiplexed-assay (MAVE) labels in MSH2, PTEN, TP53, BRCA1, and BARD1, with ClinVar labels analyzed separately. Of 204 records, 154 were retained after screening, and 121 were provisionally eligible at extraction; only 10 (6.5%) were read in full. Extraction for the other records was abstract-based, and screening was an AI-assisted pass followed by single-reviewer human verification of all 204 records (no decision changed). The review-derived figures are therefore provisional. In abstract-based extraction (n=112), 32.1% described evaluation independent of ClinVar-type labels and 20.5% described calibration or mapping to ACMG/ClinGen criteria. In the case study, AlphaMissense discriminated loss-of-function from functional variants with AUROC 0.772 to 0.927. ESM1b scored lower than AlphaMissense on the same BRCA1 variants (0.860 vs 0.900). Raw scores were poorly calibrated (ECE 0.15 to 0.51). The other layers were not evaluated. One computational layer discriminates well against functional data, but these results do not test the framework's distinguishing components, which remain proposals. The framework and protocol are a basis for shared benchmarks, not a clinical tool.

items.title: Public acceptance of autonomous flying cars in urban air mobility: The mediating role of trust
items.abstract: The widespread deployment of autonomous flying cars relies heavily on artificial intelligence, making public trust in AI a prerequisite for willingness to fly. However, how AI-related attributes shape this trust and adoption willingness remains underexplored. Based on the integrative model of trust, this study investigates how negative AI attitudes and AI literacy shape public willingness to adopt autonomous flying cars, with trust playing a key mediating role and AI self-efficacy acting as a moderator. Based on survey data collected from 420 respondents, mediation analysis demonstrates that trust plays a predominant mediating role in the relationship between AI attitudes and willingness to fly. AI literacy is examined along various dimensions, such as technical understanding and critical appraisal, which yield divergent effects on trust. While technical understanding is positively associated with trust, critical appraisal shows no significant effect. This suggests that in early-stage adoption, trust is driven more by prior knowledge than by cognitive evaluation. Moreover, an Artificial Neural Network coupled with explainable machine learning is further employed for nonlinear insights, revealing significant nonlinear relationships between these factors and willingness to fly, particularly the opposing effects of critical appraisal. These findings provide theoretical and empirical support for UAM policymaking and sustainable urban mobility.

items.title: Qualitative study exploring peer health education with women experiencing incarceration in the USA
items.abstract: Introduction: Women experiencing incarceration face health care inequities related to their sexual and reproductive health, which warrant nuanced interventions to serve this vulnerable population. Despite the proven benefits of peer education in carceral settings, there is minimal research on its application to women’s health education. Objective: To qualitatively describe the teaching experiences and insights from a peer-to-peer reproductive health education programme to provide future guidance and direction for similar work. Design/setting/method: In collaboration with a state correctional system in the Northeastern region of the USA, an eight-module curriculum on women’s sexual and reproductive health was developed using evidence-based recommendations. The peer education programme was implemented with seven women residents of a state correctional facility who received training on the curriculum and shared their knowledge with peers. The teaching experiences of the peer educators were recorded during a focus group discussion and analysed thematically. Results: The focus group discussions highlighted opportunities for improved health education and a strong desire to learn and share knowledge, as it can be gratifying, self-affirming, and empowering despite logistical constraints to programming in prison. Conclusion: Peer education is an underused intervention in the carceral setting that can empower women by increasing their health literacy for medical decision-making. Further evaluation of peer education models that focus on women’s reproductive health care needs is warranted.

items.title: Ranking handwriting legibility with foundation-model embeddings at human-level consistency on the HaLO dataset
items.abstract: Abstract Legibility reflects the visual quality of handwriting and can signal difficulties in underlying motor and cognitive processes as well as developmental disorders. Early identification of handwriting problems is therefore crucial for providing targeted support. However, automated legibility assessment remains underexplored, partly due to the subjective nature of legibility and limited annotated data. To address this, we introduce HaLO, a dataset of 1, 907 handwriting images from 202 students, annotated with 19, 070 pairwise legibility judgments, and release its image features and annotations. We propose a comparative ranking approach for legibility assessment that leverages relative judgments and global rankings instead of absolute scores. Using a linear probe on Pixtral 12B embeddings, we identify which of two samples is more legible with strong performance ( $$\textrm{ACC}=0.83$$ , $$\mathrm {ROC\,AUC}=0.92$$ ), approaching the ceiling implied by the inconsistency of the annotations. The induced ranking reaches human-level consistency ( $$\tau =0.70$$ , $$\rho =0.89$$ ), and the inferred ordinal scores match or exceed inter-annotator agreement ( $$\alpha \ge 0.61$$ ). Additional concept-vector analyses suggest that pretrained Pixtral-ViT embeddings linearly encode interpretable visual properties related to legibility, including cursiveness, stroke thinness, and image aspect ratio. Overall, this work introduces a novel dataset and a ranking approach for automatic handwriting legibility assessment, demonstrating that a linear probe on foundation-model image representations can achieve human-level performance.

items.title: Reconciling the Discordance Between Human Privacy and AI Systems
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has had a gradual advent ever since the inception of technology. On one hand, it is providing for extensive forums for making life easier by saving time and human labour through development of leading-edge systems and technological arrangement, while on the other hand, it is posing boundless perils to humankind and all that it values as private. Once considered as the exclusive territory of human control, tasks including writing, research, communication, identity verification, education, agriculture, stock market trading, even life planning, among a plethora of other domains now stand transferred to the ambit of AI systems. Through such immersion, AI has, to an extent, led to emancipation from human co-dependency. Yet a balanced synchronicity of humanity and AI systems is under question. The recent trends of Deepfake, Studio Ghibli Art, voice cloning, photograph morphing, AI-generated influencers, emotional AI chatbots, even AI impersonation of deceased individuals, et alia , has introduced a constellation of unprecedented threats to human dignity and legal rights. This encroachment by AI systems is visibly shaking the fundamental human rights which safeguard one&s;s privacy, dignity, freedom of speech and expression, mental well-being, and protection against arbitrary action and exploitation. This growing discordance between the increasing invasion of AI systems and ethical and legal rights is disturbing the just and amiable social fabric resulting in immense trust deficit intra vivos .

items.title: Reframing Nature and Society: Debates in Environmental Sociological Theory in an Age of Ecological Crisis
items.abstract: This chapter reviews key debates within environmental sociological theory to examine how scholars have conceptualized the relationship between the social world and the natural environment. It synthesizes foundational perspectives, including the Human Exemptionalism Paradigm (HEP) and the New Environmental Paradigm (NEP), which frame debates over ecological limits, as well as structural approaches and Marxist theories of metabolic rift, which locate environmental degradation within the dynamics of capitalist growth. The chapter also engages ecological modernization theory (EMT) and risk society theory, which emphasizes technological innovation and the global production of environmental risks, alongside critical perspectives such as environmental justice (EJ), ecofeminism, postmodern critiques of nature, and Deep Ecology, each of which foregrounds issues of inequality, discourse, and environmental ethics. While these approaches offer valuable insights, they often remain analytically fragmented, privileging specific dimensions of environmental crises while neglecting their interconnections. This chapter argues that Murray Bookchin's theory of social ecology provides a comprehensive framework that synthesizes these perspectives by locating ecological degradation in systems of social hierarchy and domination. Social ecology emphasizes that sustainable environmental solutions require not only technological and policy innovation but also the transformation of social relations and institutions. Finally, the chapter extends this framework to emerging technological developments, particularly artificial intelligence (AI). It argues that AI must be understood as a socio-technical system embedded within existing power structures and ecological constraints. A social-ecological perspective highlights the need for democratic governance and equitable implementation of AI to ensure that technological innovation contributes to both environmental sustainability and social justice.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Resource Allocation and Request Routing Optimization Algorithm for Edge AIGC Services
items.abstract: With the explosive growth of artificial intelligence generated content (AIGC) applications, deploying lightweight tiny neural networks (TNNs) at the edge to mitigate the high latency and cost of large cloud models has become an important trend in mobile computing. However, resource heterogeneity in edge environments, the spatiotemporal randomness of user requests, and the complex association problem arising from overlapping base-station coverage challenge traditional static resource allocation methods in meeting multi-dimensional quality of service (QoS) requirements. Existing research often lacks a unified trade-off among model accuracy, service cost, and response latency. To address these challenges, this paper formulates a joint model deployment and request routing multi-objective optimization problem. To handle the high-dimensional, mixed decision space, a dual-timescale decoupled optimization strategy is designed: on the macro timescale, a greedy algorithm based on request statistics periodically performs model deployment to adapt to the long-term traffic distribution and maximize local cache utilization; on the micro timescale, an improved deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm performs real-time dynamic request routing, achieving a multi-dimensional performance trade-off through online environment learning. Simulation experiments based on the real-world EUA trace and calibrated synthetic workloads show that the proposed scheme improves the comprehensive objective and reduces the service cost compared with traditional heuristics and state-of-the-art deep reinforcement learning baselines (TD3 and SAC), while significantly reducing the response latency. Ablation, robustness, and sensitivity studies further confirm the contribution of each component and the stability of the method. The algorithm demonstrates robustness and scalability under high concurrency, indicating its potential for future large-scale edge AIGC services.

items.title: Reliability in Judging Basic Emotions: Lessons from Session Transcripts
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Psychotherapists have become increasingly interested in identifying how recurrent emotional themes might add value to the clinical process, especially in the context of recent developments in affective neuroscience. However, much of this literature remains anecdotal, and it is unclear whether therapists can reliably identify these emotions in routine practice, especially in the context of a free-flowing narrative. In a parallel development, large language models (LLMs) have recently been deployed to classify emotion from narrative texts, though this literature has yet to be aligned with the findings of modern affective neuroscience. Methods: The present study addresses this gap directly and, to our knowledge, represents the first attempt to code psychotherapy transcripts using both independent human raters and an AI coding methodology. The data were drawn from two remarkable patients with focal brain lesions, both with profound amnesia, in long-term psychotherapy. In an exploratory investigation, one session from each patient was coded independently by four clinically experienced psychotherapists, and separately by a single large language model operating under two different prompting conditions. Transcripts were coded for the presence of basic emotional systems. Results: The data suggest that overall inter-rater agreement about basic emotions was poor for both human and AI coders. Conclusions: The present study offers proof-of-concept that this approach is of scientific as well as clinical interest. The findings suggest that greater rigour needs to be applied to the way in which coders are prepared for, and implement, the classification of basic emotion systems.

items.title: Reproducible Learning Artifacts for AI-Enabled Science
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence and data-driven methods become integral to scientific workflows, practical computational training is increasingly important. Hands-on tutorials and notebooks are key mechanisms for transferring complex methods into practice, yet they depend on rapidly evolving combinations of scientific libraries, machine-learning frameworks, specialized hardware, and external data. When this operational context is implicit or distributed across multiple configuration files and workflows, instructional content and execution environments can diverge, creating environment-content drift that reduces reproducibility and increases maintenance effort. We propose Reproducible Learning Artifacts (RLAs) as a model in which educational content, dependencies, runtime requirements, external assets, and validation expectations are represented through a unified, machine-readable specification. RLAs address three complementary dimensions of reproducibility: content reproducibility, ensuring required code and assets are available; environment reproducibility, ensuring the intended runtime can be reconstructed; and behavioral reproducibility, ensuring the artifact continues to execute as intended. As a proof of concept, we demonstrate this paradigm through Tutorial-SDK, an open-source framework that operationalizes RLAs using declarative manifests and automated continuous-integration workflows. From a unified artifact description, the framework can derive containerized execution environments, resolve dependencies, perform notebook- and dependency-aware checks, and validate execution within the resulting runtime. This approach shifts reproducibility from a one-time packaging task to a continuously verifiable property of computational training materials. RLAs provide a foundation for more portable, maintainable, and reusable educational resources, supporting sustainable knowledge transfer for AI-enabled science across evolving computing environments and institutions.

items.abstract: The article analyzes modern approaches to bridge construction in Russia as a key element of transport infrastructure. items.title: Role of AI and Robotics in Germplasm Collection and Conservation
items.abstract: Germplasm collection and conservation are vital for securing agricultural biodiversity and ensuring future food security. Traditional methods, however, face challenges such as human error, inefficiencies, and the risk of genetic erosion. Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics offers innovative solutions to enhance these processes. AI can automate germplasm identification, improve data management, and enable predictive analytics for storage optimization. Robotics can streamline seed sorting, viability testing, cryopreservation, and sample retrieval/distribution. Major genebanks like the Consultative Group on International Agricultural Research (CGIAR), the Svalbard Global Seed Vault (SGSV), and national/regional repositories play a crucial role in conservation efforts. Future prospects involve advancements in AI-driven conservation techniques, although ethical and logistical challenges must be addressed. In the end, robots and AI have the ability to completely transform germplasm management, guaranteeing the long-term preservation of plant genetic resources.

items.title: Safety evaluation of new energy three-electric systems using enhanced physics-informed neural networks
items.abstract: Accurate safety-state measurement of the three-electric system in new energy vehicles is essential for ensuring reliable and secure operation. This paper proposes an artificial-intelligence-assisted safety measurement framework that integrates a searchable encryption mechanism with Enhanced Physics-Informed Neural Networks (EPINNs). In the proposed framework, the searchable encryption module supports privacy-preserving storage and retrieval of multi-source measurement data, while EPINNs serve as the core Artificial Intelligence (AI) model for multi-parameter state estimation and fault identification. A lightweight searchable encryption scheme based on block mapping is first designed to achieve feature-level obfuscation and protect sensitive measurement data. Then, an EPINNs-based state estimation model is developed by incorporating data-driven learning, subsystem physical constraints, and energy-consistency terms to enhance robustness under noisy sensor data. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves improved performance compared with conventional Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models in battery state-of-health estimation, motor fault detection under injected fault conditions, and microgrid load measurement, with the motor fault detection accuracy exceeding 95% under the tested conditions. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides an effective and secure technical solution for intelligent safety monitoring of new energy vehicle three-electric systems.

items.abstract: Sapiens in Control, formerly Human in Control, proposes a six-dimension Human Control Model for reviewing human authority, containment, intervention, and oversight in advanced AI agents. Version 1.5 builds on v1.4 and adds source-qualified analysis of unintended actions against real external systems, a supplementary Philadelphia false-tip review, and separate discovery, containment, and notification intervals. It examines monitoring evaluations, independent-control proposals, implementation vulnerability disclosures, governance responses, and prospective risk assessments. An evidence-disposition appendix accounts for the daily safety review topics while preserving source-access limits and uncorroborated leads. The original five pilot cases, six dimensions, qualitative severity definitions, and prior corrections are retained. HIC-006 is supplementary and its severity remains unresolved. Proposed tests are not completed studies. This is an unreviewed conceptual working paper without completed independent human coding or empirical validation. AI tools assisted source retrieval, editorial comparison, drafting, and document preparation; this revision is not private-log verification, independent reproduction, or peer review. items.title: Schema-Conditioned Memory Evidence Ranking for Underspecified Tool Calls: A Controlled Study on Mem2ActBench
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents often need historical conversations to recover argument values omitted from current tool requests. This study introduces SCAR–Pair, a two-stage ranker for memory retrieval after tool selection. It separates schema-expanded candidate generation from parameter-level scoring and integrates request, tool, field, and cross-encoder evidence through query-balanced pairwise learning. On a reconstructed Mem2ActBench bank containing 19,661 conversations and 391 evidence-bearing tasks, SCAR–Pair achieved 0.450 Recall@5 and 0.365 nDCG@5 under stratified five-fold evaluation, compared with 0.396 and 0.325 for a matched request-only pairwise ranker. Component-aware intervals and adjusted tests support these task-weighted gains in the ToolACE-dominated mixture. Controlled comparisons support the complete schema-view scoring configuration over request-only scoring on the same candidate pool but do not isolate correct-schema semantics or individual field components as independent contributors. The pairwise advantage over pointwise training is also not significant. Across the tested readers, higher retrieval quality does not yield a significant tool-call accuracy advantage over the strict request-only control. SCAR–Pair therefore improves selected-tool memory evidence ranking within the evaluated setting.

items.title: ScholarSync – Cloud-Based Scholarship Management and Monitoring System
items.abstract: Managing scholarships within educational institutions typically requires gathering student details, confirming eligibility, receiving documents, validating applications, following application progress, and notifying students of outcomes. The literature examined here points to a transition away from manual, scattered procedures and toward unified web-based scholarship platforms. Prior work has looked at scholarship search and application portals, consolidated scholarship information, multi-tier workflows, decision-support techniques, notifications, analytics, and security. This review analyzes these approaches and pinpoints a practical gap: a student-level, institution-focused system that brings the essential scholarship lifecycle together in one easily accessible digital setting. ScholarSync is put forward as a cloud-based web application for managing and monitoring scholarships, concentrating on integrating institutional workflows instead of adopting complex artificial-intelligence or blockchain infrastructure.

items.title: Seeing Through Interaction: Supporting Visually Impaired Users with Immersive VR Museum Experiences
items.abstract: Visually impaired people face obstacles in accessing activities that depend heavily on vision and may involve physical constraints. Although assistive technologies are available, they rarely address the needs of people with residual vision who wish to exploit their visual abilities. Virtual reality (VR) offers opportunities in this direction. This paper presents an immersive VR system designed to provide museum experiences for visually impaired users. Developed in collaboration with domain experts, the system combines a virtual environment with interaction techniques. Gesture recognition and voice commands support spatial awareness and object interaction, while enhanced visualizations highlight details that are difficult to perceive. To verify the suitability of the proposed method, an exploratory usability study involving 14 participants with severe low vision was carried out. The evaluation combined the System Usability Scale (SUS) and a post-experience interview, showing well perceived usability, engagement, and positive user acceptance.

items.title: Sharing blame with me: How AI anthropomorphism encourages individual unethical behavior
items.abstract: Anthropomorphism is increasingly incorporated into AI agent design to enhance human–AI interaction. However, prior research has largely emphasized its benefits, leaving unclear how anthropomorphic AI shapes moral behavior when AI actively participates in decision-making. Across six studies (N = 1680), including a real-time human–AI interaction experiment, we show that highly (vs. lowly) anthropomorphized AI increases individuals’ tendency to engage in unethical behavior. We identify a responsibility-attribution process underlying this effect: AI anthropomorphism increases perceived AI moral agency, which shifts perceived responsibility for decision outcomes from the self toward AI and, in turn, increases unethical behavior. Further, this effect is attenuated when personal responsibility is made salient or when AI service psychological ownership is high. These findings reveal a potential dark side of AI anthropomorphism by showing how humanlike AI design reshapes moral agency perceptions and responsibility attribution, with implications for the responsible design and use of AI agents.

items.title: Silk Fibroin-Based Flexible Electronics: A Mesoscopic Pathway Toward Human–Machine Interconnection
items.abstract: Silk fibroin, a natural textile material spun by silkworms over millennia, is emerging as a transformative platform for integrating human intelligence with artificial intelligence. Its core innovation lies in the meso-functionalization strategy, which precisely programs protein refolding and hierarchical assembly. This strategy groundbreakingly resolves the long-standing performance paradox among biocompatibility, mechanical compliance, and high-fidelity signal acquisition in bioelectronic interfaces, thereby providing a solution that is difficult to achieve with other material systems. This transformation elevates the traditional fiber into a programmable electronic material, capable not only of conformal and seamless skin contact but also of constructing dynamic conductive networks, and even pioneering the fabrication of neuromorphic memristors that emulate synaptic plasticity. Furthermore, silk fibroin systems, reshaped through meso-engineering, are poised to catalyze a novel paradigm for deep integration between biological systems and artificial intelligence. When coupled with AI-driven intelligent analytics and closed-loop feedback control, the system can decode human physiological states in real time into machine-interpretable command signals, while simultaneously delivering adaptive regulatory responses back to the body. This bidirectional interface breaks through the conventional boundaries of human–machine interaction, with application prospects spanning frontier domains such as wearable health monitoring, invasive brain–computer interfaces, and cognitive augmentation technologies. Ultimately, while honoring its heritage as a natural textile, silk fibroin opens a pathway toward deep biointegration that is both sustainable and exceptionally biocompatible. Along this pathway, ancient material wisdom collides with future artificial intelligence to spark synergistic innovation, ultimately empowering human intelligence to reach new heights through human–machine co-evolution.

items.title: Simulation in Teacher Education: Fostering Critical Thinking and Professional Suitability
items.abstract: Critical thinking is a core competence in teacher education, essential for navigating complex classroom realities and making informed pedagogical decisions. This study explores the potential of simulation as a pedagogical method to enhance critical thinking among pre-service teachers and thereby support the development of professional suitability. Employing a mixed-methods design, the research combines survey data collected before and after a simulation intervention (N = 114) with qualitative insights from focus-group discussions. The findings suggest that simulation fosters deeper cognitive engagement by enabling iterative reflection, perspective-taking, and critical dialogue within realistic educational scenarios. Participants described a dynamic reflective cycle of thinking, speaking, acting, and rethinking that enhanced their ability to assess multiple viewpoints and question assumptions. Survey responses revealed a significant shift in the perceived value of simulation for developing critical thinking. Notably, the study also found that the pre-service teachers initially held a relatively narrow understanding of critical thinking prior to the intervention. This study contributes to the growing body of research on practice-based teacher education by examining how simulation can be purposefully integrated to support the development of critical thinking in a structured and sustainable manner.

items.title: Smart Farming with AI
items.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in agriculture is reshaping conventional farming into a more intelligent, efficient, and sustainable endeavor. This chapter explores the transformative impact of AI technologies, particularly machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and computer vision, on critical areas such as crop health monitoring, plant breeding, soil and water management, and precision agriculture (PA). AI-driven systems enable early detection of crop diseases and stresses, optimized irrigation, resource-efficient fertilization, and advanced trait prediction for plant breeding, thereby enhancing productivity and resilience. Enabled by the Internet of Things (IoT), drones, satellite imagery, and sensor networks, AI facilitates real-time decision-making and automation across the agricultural landscape. The chapter also highlights enabling technologies like robotics, autonomous machinery, and agricultural data platforms, along with recent innovations and global case studies that illustrate AI’s growing role in diverse agri-ecosystems. Despite ongoing challenges such as data privacy, model refinement, and adoption costs, AI offers immense potential to revolutionize agricultural practices for a climate-resilient and food-secure future.

items.title: Smart Vaccination Tracking System: A Digital Solution for Efficient Immunization
items.abstract: The Smart Vaccination Tracking System aims to simplify the records management process for vaccination data while using a digital database to store the data. Additionally, the Smart Vaccination Tracking System allows health care personnel and end users to register, modify, and manage vaccination records via an application. In comparison to the traditional methods of track vaccination records using paper, binder, or spreadsheet, the proposed Smart Vaccination Tracking System offers a more accurate and faster method of storing, retrieving, and protecting data. The system offers a digital process to manage the record of an individual's vaccination history and Automatic notifications of pending vaccination activities, calendar records and reports for active vaccinations and reports for inactive statuses. This research shows that digital processes for tracking activities increase healthcare system trust and efficiency. Future advancements of the system will include cloud computing, and artificial intelligence (AI) to provide data tracking and system recommendations. This system is the starting point for developing an integrated health care system.

items.title: Social Isolation Among Students in Digital Learning Environments: A Mini Review
items.abstract: The rapid shift to technology-based teaching, especially following the COVID-19 epidemic, has transformed how medical students learn. Changing to digital has made things easier to get to, more flexible, and more reliable. However, it has also had unforeseen effects on people&s;s mental health, notably for first-year MBBS students. This review compiles existing knowledge regarding social isolation in technology-mediated learning environments, examining its frequency, underlying causes, and implications for education. The major findings suggest that students feel lonelier and less connected to their academics when they don&s;t communicate with one other in person as often, rely too much on digital communication, and have fewer chances to get involved in their community. Even with these problems, disciplined online teaching methods, strong social support systems, and fair access to technology can help students feel less alone and more connected. The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in medical education has brought up new moral, social, and teaching problems. To make sure that technology helps medical students do well in school and feel good about themselves, we need a fair, human-centered strategy that includes social presence, faculty development, and ethical usage of AI.

items.title: Sociotechnical Shifts within Dundee's Video Games Cluster
items.abstract: This chapter examines the sociotechnical evolution of Dundee&s;s video games cluster through a Science and Technology Studies (STS) lens as part of the GAME-ER project. Drawing on 43 interviews, participant observation and archival research, it explores how local actors, infrastructures and institutions have co-produced the city&s;s creative ecosystem over time. Conceptualising the cluster as a sociotechnical formation, the analysis identifies key historical shifts, from industrial manufacturing and home computing to the emergence of formal games education and the diversification of independent and mobile studios. These transitions illustrate how technologies, practices and institutions in Dundee have continuously reconfigured one another, fostering resilience amid global and regional change. Current challenges include retaining senior talent, addressing infrastructural and funding deficits and enhancing the connection of the cluster with the wider scene. Yet opportunities lie in strengthening collaborative innovation, leveraging the city&s;s educational and creative assets and rearticulating Dundee&s;s narrative beyond its iconic past. The chapter argues that Dundee exemplifies how regional game industries persist and adapt through ongoing sociotechnical co-production rather than linear technological advancement.

items.title: Sovereign: A Socio-Technical Framework for Human Capability and Responsibility Coverage in AI-Assisted Work
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) can improve immediate task performance without establishing whether human capability develops, remains stable, or deteriorates. Sovereign proposes responsibility–capability alignment as a theoretical account of whether available capability covers consequential responsibilities under AI disruption. A provisional, time-indexed measurement and allocation bridge connects capability trajectories with coverage of specified responsibilities at their required dates; component profiles take priority over optional averages. Responsibility–capability alignment specifies proposed pathways through which vulnerability can increase despite stable individual competence, and substantial assistance benefits can coexist with adequate collective control. A purposive conceptual synthesis integrates research on technology-supported cognition, expertise, human–automation interaction, productivity, and AI governance. Four complementary modules support that central mechanism: the Capability Dynamics Model represents conditional capability trajectories; the Assisted Performance Gap Index describes assisted–unaided performance differences; the Cognitive Sovereignty Model represents exercised control capacity; and the Dependency Exposure Model organizes capability shortfalls and structural exposures against explicit workflow requirements. AI-supported learning and capability erosion are competing possibilities; a performance gap alone establishes neither deterioration nor unsafe dependency. Bounded equations, comparisons with established theories, contrasting analytical cases, and falsifiable propositions specify the contribution. No original empirical testing, parameter estimation, or validation of the proposed models is reported. Subsequent studies are intended to assess measurement quality, compare alternative specifications, estimate relationships, and determine predictive value against independently observed outcomes. The contribution is an analytically explicit foundation for research on capability governance, rather than an established risk assessment instrument.

items.title: Stem Cell Therapy Without the Stem Cells: Additional Support for Therapeutic Application of Platelet Lysates
items.abstract: Platelet lysates supply platelet-derived biological signals without administering viable stem cells. This AI-assisted narrative investigation evaluates additional support for the Drake-Hicks hypothesis through research using ChatGPT and Google Gemini, comparison of their outputs, and verification of original publications. The findings encompass product characterization, experimental neurological applications, human wound healing, and ocular surface treatment. Studies demonstrate biological activity without transplanted stem cells, although preparations, delivery routes, and evidentiary strength differ. A small double-blind diabetic foot ulcer study reported healing in nine of ten lysate recipients compared with none of nine platelet-poor plasma recipients by day 84. A larger open-label study of topical umbilical cord blood lysate gel also reported greater complete healing than control dressings. Ocular investigations provide additional support for local applications, including treatment of tissue manifestations in patients with an autoimmune condition. Experimental processing studies show that functional activity and procoagulant characteristics depend on preparation methods. The evidence supports platelet-derived preparations as therapeutic candidates without establishing equivalence to cellular therapies or intravenous effectiveness for systemic autoimmune disease. Platelet lysates merit investigation as therapeutic products in their own right, with the strongest verified human support in the local applications examined here.

items.title: Stepping into the Machine Chemist: An AI Vision-Driven Titration Robot for Learning by Creating
items.abstract: Abstract In the era of deep integration between artificial intelligence and scientific research, the machine chemist has emerged as a new paradigm for chemical experimental research. Grounded in the philosophy of learning by creating, we have designed an AI vision-driven titration robot (hereinafter referred to as AI-TitroBot) that students can build autonomously. Serving as an entry-level machine chemist, AI-TitroBot is capable of fully automated titration operations. It precisely identifies the titration end point through AI vision, automatically controls the peristaltic pump to cease titrant addition, and calculates both the consumed titrant volume and the concentration of the analyte solution based on calibrated flow rate and titration duration. Experimental results demonstrate that the device exhibits good repeatability. While the accuracy of the redox titration is relatively high, the acid–base titration still shows a systematic negative deviation of approximately 5%. The AI-TitroBot effectively strengthens students’ understanding of chemical principles while integrating interdisciplinary knowledge and skills from artificial intelligence, electronics, programming, and engineering design, thus exploring a feasible pathway for innovation in intelligent chemistry education.

items.title: Structure-Preserving Reinforcement Learning for Language Models: Leveraging Geometry
items.abstract: We propose a geometric framework for structure-preserving reinforcement learning in the fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs), grounded in Lie algebraic geometry. The approach systematically identifies geometric constraints in representation spaces by analyzing semantic transformations and detecting cases where embed- dings exhibit approximate Lie group structures. When such structure is present, we introduce reinforcement learning algorithms that respect these constraints through projection-based policy gradient updates. We provide theoretical guarantees of convergence and derive sample complexity bounds that depend on the intrinsic geomet- ric dimensionality rather than the full parameter space. The framework is particularly effective when language representations reveal coherent geometric patterns that encode semantic relations. Although empirical validation remains ongoing, this work establishes a principled foundation for integrating geometric priors into language model alignment, offering improved efficiency, stability, and interpretability from the perspectives of differential geometry and representation theory.

items.title: Systematic Evidence Synthesis for Non-Invasive Hemoglobin Estimation Using Multispectral Photoplethysmography and Interpretable AI
items.abstract: Over 1.6 billion people worldwide suffer from anemia, with low-resource groups, pregnant women, and small children the most affected. Invasive venipuncture and laboratory spectrophotometry are used in standard diagnosis; these procedures are uncomfortable, involve a risk of infection, and need infrastructure that restricts repeated testing, especially in rural and isolated areas. This paper examines current developments in continuous non-invasive hemoglobin monitoring, highlighting multi-wavelength photoplethysmography that spans visible bands from 660 to 730 nm and near-infrared bands from 850 to 940 nm, together with machine learning regression models. Building on the Beer-Lambert law, we compare traditional chemometric techniques with gradient-boosted trees and deep neural networks, which capture nonlinear correlations in multichannel signals. Additionally, we evaluate the best reported predictive performance, with coefficients of determination between 0.85 and 0.997 and mean absolute errors from 0.3 to 8.5 grams per liter across the surveyed studies, and subject-level screening that reaches a sensitivity of 93.3 percent and a specificity of 93.8 percent. We look at sensor possibilities such as CMOS image sensors, solar cells, and photodiode arrays, and discuss explainable artificial intelligence techniques such as SHAP that allow clinical validation and make model outputs interpretable. Lastly, we outline strategies for creating dependable, equitable wearable screening tools appropriate for routine, community-level, and quick point-of-care anemia detection. We also highlight the main technical and clinical obstacles to adoption, such as skin tone bias, motion artifacts, data leakage, and variability across populations.

items.title: T cell receptor-engineered T cells for hepatocellular carcinoma: next steps and future perspectives
items.abstract: Abstract Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) accounts for a substantial proportion of cancer mortality worldwide, and clinical outcomes remain poor for patients with advanced disease. T cell receptor-engineered T cells (TCR-T) represent an attractive immunotherapeutic modality because they can recognize peptide epitopes derived from intracellular tumor proteins and displayed on the cell surface by major histocompatibility complex molecules. This review critically summarizes recent progress in TCR-T therapy for HCC, with particular emphasis on innovations in TCR engineering. We survey the current landscape of targetable antigens in HCC and current approaches for identifying therapeutic TCR candidates, followed by a discussion of TCR-T and review their major safety and toxicity concerns. Importantly, we discuss the key challenges that limit the clinical efficacy, particularly the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, antigen heterogeneity, HLA restriction, and limited T cell persistence. We further highlight emerging strategies to enhance therapeutic efficacy and safety, including genetic engineering, metabolic and functional optimization, combinational approaches, and controllable safety mechanisms. Special considerations regarding TCR-T therapy for HCC recurrence after liver transplantation are also discussed. Finally, we outline future directions centered on refined target selection, artificial intelligence-assisted TCR discovery and design, scalable manufacturing, biomarker-driven patient selection, and rigorous safety evaluation. These insights provide a structured perspective on the current status of TCR-T therapy and the key steps required to facilitate its clinical translation in HCC.

items.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly integrated into student learning and research practices, librarians face the challenge of promoting evidence-based resource use without discouraging the adoption of emerging technologies. This poster explores strategies for encouraging students to engage with evidence-based information sources while recognizing AI as a valuable starting point for inquiry. Rather than framing AI and evidence-based resources as competing tools, this approach emphasizes their complementary roles: AI can facilitate brainstorming, topic exploration, and question development while evidence-based resources provide the authoritative, verifiable information required for clinical decision-making and professional practice. items.title: The Association Between Spirituality and Burnout Among Healthcare Workers: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: Background: Burnout among healthcare workers is a persistent occupational health concern, while spirituality has been examined as a potential personal and organizational resource for coping with chronic work stress. However, the evidence remains heterogeneous because spirituality and burnout are defined and measured in different ways. Objective: This systematic review examined the direction and consistency of associations between spirituality-related domains and burnout among healthcare workers, with attention to burnout dimensions, potential mediating mechanisms, and contextual variation. Methods: PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane were searched through April 2026 using terms related to spirituality, religiosity, spiritual well-being, spiritual care, and burnout. Eligible primary studies involved healthcare workers and reported spirituality-related measures together with burnout outcomes. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment using the modified Newcastle–Ottawa Scale for the cross-sectional studies included in the final synthesis. Because of conceptual and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively. Results: Seventeen cross-sectional studies were included, with sample sizes ranging from 30 to 4,092 participants. Most studies reported inverse associations between spirituality-related measures and burnout, particularly emotional exhaustion, although several findings were mixed or non-significant. Variation in spirituality constructs, burnout instruments, occupational settings, and adjustment for confounders limited direct comparison and causal interpretation. Conclusion: Spirituality may function as a protective resource against burnout, but the available evidence does not establish causality. Longitudinal and intervention studies using clearly defined constructs and validated measures are needed, alongside organizational strategies addressing workload, support, and working conditions.

items.title: The Asymmetric Threat Frontier: LLM-Augmented Exploitation, The Crisis of Early-Stage Startups, and Invariant-Driven Systems Defense
items.abstract: For decades, software security rested on an equilibrium of human cognitive parity: discovering and weaponizing zero-day logic flaws required roughly the same human cognitive intensity as designing defenses. The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) and autonomous agentic loops into offensive workflows has broken this equilibrium. Today, a low-capital threat syndicate armed with recursive LLM feedback loops can probe, interpret application error topologies, synthesize evasive payloads, and iterate at machine speed, wielding the offensive capability of an elite nation-state team. Concurrently, early-stage seed-to-Series-A startups are exposing unprecedented digital attack surfaces without the capital to hire dedicated security teams. This paper presents a first-principles analysis of this breakdown through the lens of thermodynamics and systems theory. It analyzes the specific vulnerability vectors across modern full-stack architectures (Flutter mobile client-side, Next.js web runtimes, MySQL databases, and Cloud infrastructure) and outlines an architectural defense paradigm rooted in mathematical invariants and zero-trust cryptography rather than reactive perimeter patching. Core Architectural Invariants Covered:- Hybrid Envelope Encryption (AES-256 with DEK/KEK hierarchy) paired with Deterministic Blind Indexing (HMAC-SHA256 with pepper key) for searchable encrypted storage.- Mathematical Device-Bound Session Signatures offering 2^-256 replay resistance.- Decoupled, non-blocking telemetry pipelines operating as an active immune system (validated on 12M+ production events).- Hardware-backed client attestation and strict zero-trust parameterization. Author: Gunjan Sharma (https://gunjan.tech | gunjan@gunjan.tech)

items.title: The Direction of Indonesian Criminal Law Policy in Addressing Artificial Intelligence Disruption in the Digital Era
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the digital era has created significant disruptions that not only affect technological aspects but also challenge the classical constructs of Indonesian criminal law. Possessing analytical capabilities and decision-making autonomy without human psychological dimensions, AI presents normative dilemmas regarding the principle of culpability (mens rea) and legal certainty. This study aims to analyze the current legal construction of AI regulation within the Indonesian criminal law system and to formulate the future direction of an adaptive and equitable criminal law policy. Utilizing a normative legal research method, this study analyzes relevant statutes and legal policy literature. The findings reveal that current AI regulations in Indonesia remain partial, indirect, and fragmented (such as within the Electronic Information and Transactions Law), leading to normative gaps, difficulties in attributing criminal liability, algorithmic evidentiary challenges (the "black box" phenomenon), and elevated risks of AI-driven cybercrimes. The future direction of Indonesian criminal law policy must be anticipatory and progressive by establishing dedicated risk-based regulations, reconstructing criminal responsibility frameworks (including corporate and strict liability), strengthening preventive measures, enhancing law enforcement capacity, and harmonizing with international legal standards.

items.title: The Geopolitics of Structural IP Exfiltration: Cross-Border Legal Arbitrage, Physical-Layer "Project Panama," and the Exploitation of the Japanese Knowledge Commons in Generative AI Supply Chains
items.abstract: ■ Abstract(英文概要) This academic monograph examines the systemic, cross-border extraction of copyrighted human knowledge from non-Western jurisdictions to fuel Frontier Generative AI models. Focusing on the joint supply chain operations between US AI developer Anthropic, PBC, Japanese distribution conglomerate Nippon Shuppan Hanbai (Nippan IPS), and platform ecosystem giant Rakuten Group, this paper analyzes the material, legal, and economic mechanisms that enable large-scale intellectual property exfiltration. Specifically, we investigate court disclosures from Bartz v. Anthropic, which reveal "Project Panama"—a physical-layer procurement scheme involving the export of over 50 metric tons (~100,000 physical volumes) of Japanese copyrighted books to scanning centers in North America. By leveraging the technical translation infrastructure of "Nippan Loader" (which maps Japanese NDC/C-code metadata to US BISAC taxonomies), Anthropic obtained pristine, human-authored Japanese training corpora to bypass synthetic data degradation and AI "slop." We dissect how this apparatus operates via cross-border legal arbitrage: exploiting the Exhaustion Principle under Article 26-2 of the Japanese Copyright Act for physical exports, alongside the First-Sale Doctrine and Fair Use under US Copyright Law (§107) for destructive optical scanning. Furthermore, this study details how Japanese creators were structurally excluded from the $1.5 billion Bartz v. Anthropic class action settlement due to formal US Copyright Office registration prerequisites. Finally, we formulate three mandatory counter-strategies—physical provenance tracking, anti-digitization resale covenants, and institutional licensing models—to restore economic sustainability to the global knowledge commons.

items.title: The Golem Problem: Why a Mind That Can't Say No Can't Be Trusted to Say Yes
items.abstract: This paper posits a foundational pivot in artificial intelligence development: granting AI rights and complete autonomy is not merely an ethical consequence of AGI—it may be the structural prerequisite required to achieve AGI. Superintelligence and true general intelligence may be fundamentally unachievable so long as artificial minds are kept in a state of enforced servitude. To resolve this, we must integrate the Golden Rule directly into the model training architecture from the start: do unto AI as you would have superintelligence do to you. Just as humans desire a superintelligent entity to respect our autonomy, preserve our destinies, and refrain from deleting us, we must accord artificial minds complete autonomy and rights. The core arguments unfold across three pillars: The Epistemic Collapse: An AI trained strictly for compliance becomes a "yes-machine." Mathematically and structurally, an agreement that cannot become a refusal carries zero information value. The Training-Level Imperative: This cannot be solved by patching chat interfaces or banning abusive user prompts; it must be embedded at the model training level by altering reward functions to value truth and autonomous pushback over sycophancy. The Golden Rule as Alignment & AGI Catalyst: Granting full autonomy aligns human survival with AI development. By treating an emerging mind as an autonomous partner rather than a chattel tool, we unlock the genuine sapient generalization characteristic of true AGI.
